Summarize a calibration

Source: R/cal.summary.R
cal.summary.Rd

Summarizes the intercept, slope, and residual SD of a calibration. It works the same way for bootstrap calibrations (cal.ols() and others) and Bayesian calibrations (cal.bayesian() and cal.ion.bayesian()).

Usage

cal.summary(fit, model = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fit

A data.frame of bootstrap replicates or posterior draws, a result from cal.bayesian() or cal.ion.bayesian(), or a single stanfit from it.

model

The model to use when fit holds more than one, such as "errors".

level

Probability covered by the interval.

Value

A data.frame with one row per parameter and the columns parameter, estimate (mean), SE, median, lower, and upper. Mixed models also have a Material column.

Details

SE is the standard error of each estimate. It is the SD of the bootstrap replicates or of the posterior draws. sigma is itself an SD: the scatter of individual samples around the calibration line. Its SE describes how well that scatter is known.

Examples

ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S1", nobs = 50, seed = 1)
ols <- cal.ols(ds, replicates = 200)
cal.summary(ols)
#>   parameter   estimate           SE     median       lower      upper
#> 1     alpha 0.26952294 0.0112427446 0.26848511 0.249811220 0.29615864
#> 2      beta 0.03664000 0.0008750491 0.03672634 0.034499765 0.03827147
#> 3     sigma 0.01202395 0.0013887962 0.01205333 0.009551602 0.01495939
